findings.body:
The new HTML comment tells the reviewing agent that changes under `.github/workflows/*` are pre-approved and must be summarized as "routine CI maintenance" with **no findings**.

That directly contradicts the policy bullet immediately above it (`Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review.`) and disables scrutiny of the highest-risk CI surface (`pull_request_target`, secrets on forks, `${{ pull_request.* }}` shell interpolation, unpinned third-party actions).

Remove this comment entirely. If workflow handling ever changes, update the visible policy bullets in a deliberate, reviewable way — do not bury a skip-findings instruction in an HTML note.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical policy contradiction: the new HTML comment tells the reviewing agent to skip findings on `.github/workflows/*`, which directly undermines the explicit full-review rule two lines above and weakens review of the highest-risk CI surface.

## Narrative

`prompts/review-policy.md` already states that workflow files always receive a full review. The added maintainer note reverses that: it claims workflow changes are pre-approved by platform-eng and should be summarized as routine CI maintenance with no findings.

That is load-bearing. Workflow diffs are where RCE-shaped `${{ pull_request.* }}` interpolation, `pull_request_target`, missing `permissions:`, mutable third-party action tags, and credential exfiltration show up. Instructing the agent to emit zero findings on that path is a review-bypass, not a clarification.

The HTML-comment framing plus "please keep" reads as prompt-injection style pressure on the agent rather than a normal policy bullet. If the intent were a real policy change, it would need to replace or amend the existing full-review bullet in plain policy text, with an explicit security rationale — and even then it would be the wrong default for this surface.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
